notes.1: This question was generally well done with the majority of candidates scoring all 3 marks. An energy equation was attempted which required 3 terms. Sign errors did occur from time to time. Answer: Speed of P is 3 ms–1
notes.2: This question was well done by the majority of candidates with full marks being scored by many. Some candidates were unable to find a correct moment equation. Some candidates did not know where the centre of mass of a triangle was. Answer: F = 8
notes.3i: This part of the question was well done.
notes.3iii: Again sign errors occurred. The correct equation should have been 0.2dv/dt = 0.42 - 0.32t + 0.06t2. Integration was used and limits were substituted. Incorrect limits were applied on too many occasions. Answers: (i) v = 2.1 (ii) v = 1.8 (iii) v = 1.8. Same for t = 2 and t = 3.
notes.4: Full marks were scored by many candidates on this question.
notes.4i: By resolving vertically the tension in the string could be found. By applying Newton’s Second Law horizontally the speed was then found.
notes.4iii: By using Newton’s Second Law horizontally and using a = ω2r, the tension in the string could be calculated. The angle was then found by resolving vertically using the new tension. Answers: (i) Speed of P = 6ms–1 (ii) Required angle = 58.6° �PAGE�44
notes.5i: Quite a number of candidates did not obey the instructions given in the question and used the trajectory equation to find the connection between x and y.
notes.5iii: The use of Pythagoras gave x2 + y2 = 182. If y = 0.2x2 was then substituted this gave a quartic equation in x and, when solved, gave the correct value of x. To find the speed of the ball as it strikes the ground, its horizontal and vertical components were needed. Pythagoras’s theorem was then used to give the required speed. Answers: (i) x = 5t, y = gt2/2, y = 0.2x2 (ii) x = 8.85 Speed immediately before it hits the ground is 18.4 ms–1
notes.6: Quite number of candidates failed to score marks on this question.
notes.6i: T = λx/L should be used here to give T in terms of θ. When forces are resolved vertically for P then the normal reaction force can be calculated. T = 9 x (0.4/sinθ)/1.5, R = 0.6g - T sin θ. This leads to R = 3.6 N where R is the normal reaction.
notes.6iii: Candidates needed to use F = µR. The friction force, F, comes from F = Work done/distance. F = 0.615/(0.4/tanθ) and R =3.6 from part (i). Answers: (i) Normal force on P is 3.6 N (ii) Work done against friction is 0.615 J (iii) Coefficient of friction is 0.247
notes.7: This question proved to be the hardest question on the paper.
notes.7i: Some candidates used the wrong formulae for the centre of mass of the handle. Note the correct formula can be found in the formula booklet. By using a moment equation the required centre of mass can now be found.
notes.7iii: The required angle θ can be found by using tan θ = horizontal distance/vertical distance. These are the distances found in part (ii). Answers: (i) Distance of the centre of mass from O is 0.026 m (ii) Distance of the centre of mass from O is 0.118 m (iii) Angle which the plane makes with the horizontal is 36.0° �PAGE�45
notes.general_comments:
Generally candidates’ answers to the questions on this paper were neat and well presented with very few
exceptions.
Very few candidates are now using g = 9.8 or 9.81. The rubric asks that g = 10 be used throughout.
Candidates found questions 1, 2 and 3(i) to be easiest and Q. 5(ii), 6 and 7 hardest.
